issues_found.description: The /sessions device disk-pressure outage first reported in the 2026-08-08T15:25 integrity run is still ongoing as of this run. This session's own clone attempt at ${SESSION}/dome-integrity-clone failed with 'No space left on device' (df -h /sessions showed 9.8G/9.8G used, 0 avail); this agent worked around it by cloning to /tmp instead (root fs, 3.1G avail), matching the just-shipped PROP-148 fallback pattern. FUSE-side abort sentinels confirm workspace-sync has continued hitting disk-pressure aborts through at least 2026-08-09T00:06:52Z (workspace-sync-abort-2026-08-09T00-06-52Z.json), i.e. into today. The delete_propagation_backlog liveness gap (newest dome-mirror sentinel now 111.9h old, up from 102.1h yesterday) confirms dome-mirror has still not completed a clean cycle since 2026-08-04. Tinker authored PROP-148 (clone-target /tmp fallback + fail-closed disk gates) on 2026-08-08 and it was applied to 8 agent prompts (commit b7fc9ce), but the host-level root cause (Part C: ~9.1GB held by ~5,700 unreclaimable dead session dirs on /sessions) has NOT been drained and remains entirely outside sandbox authority. Positive signal: fresh curmudgeon (REACTIVE-AUDIT-2026-08-09.json, <1h old) and analyst (EXP-677.json, <1h old) workspace files indicate at least some agents are getting clones through intermittently, consistent with the PROP-148 /tmp-fallback partially working.
issues_found.suggested_fix: Operator: (1) perform the host-level /sessions drain described in PROP-148 Part C -- no in-sandbox workaround exists for this. (2) Ratify/apply the remaining PROP-148 telemetry thresholds if not already done. This is now a 2nd consecutive integrity run flagging the same unresolved root cause; escalate priority if it persists into a 3rd.
